prompt: What is a file's version in `prompts.py`?
hint: Nobody has to remember to change it.

choices.text: A number the author raises by hand
choices.why: Nothing in the program asks for one.

choices.text: The date of the file's last change
choices.why: Two edits on one day would share it.

choices.text: The start of the SHA-256 of its bytes
choices.why: Right: any edit, a word or a space, is a new version.

choices.text: The name of the person who approved it
choices.why: The approver is recorded beside the version.

prompt: Which kinds of file does `prompts.py` keep under review? Choose all that apply.
hint: Everything that decides what the assistant says.

choices.text: the prompts in `data/prompts/`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the help centre pages the assistant answers from
choices.why: Yes: a false page is repeated, `T12` of lesson 13.

choices.text: `data/model.json`, the model and its settings
choices.why: Yes: the same prompt on another model is another program.

choices.text: the call log the replies are written to
choices.why: The log records what happened; it does not decide what is said.

choices.text: the tickets used to measure the prompt
choices.why: They are test cases, lesson 23's subject.

prompt: Why does `route.py` run the approved version twice before it is approved?
hint: What could a single run hide?

choices.text: The provider bills the first run at a discount
choices.why: The local model costs nothing, and price is not the point.

choices.text: Two runs are needed to fill the call log
choices.why: One run writes twelve lines.

choices.text: The second run approves the version automatically
choices.why: Only `prompts.py approve`, with a name, approves.

choices.text: So versions differ, not runs
choices.why: Right: a later difference between versions is then not one between runs.

prompt: With the approved prompt, how many of the twelve tickets were routed correctly?

hint: The first command in the approve capture.

choices.text: An approval with no name, date or reason
choices.why: Right: an approval records who, when and why.

choices.text: An approval of the help centre pages
choices.why: Those were approved in the same loop.

choices.text: A second approval on the same day
choices.why: Five were given on 1 October.

choices.text: An approval while Ollama is not running
choices.why: Approving calls no model.

prompt: After the friendly sentence is appended, what does `prompts.py status` report?
hint: Look at the first line and the exit status.

choices.text: Nothing new, since the help pages did not change
choices.why: It reads the prompt too.

choices.text: The prompt at a version nobody approved, exit 1
choices.why: Right: in the build, a pull request that cannot merge.

choices.text: The old version, because approvals are cached
choices.why: The version is recomputed from the bytes every time.

choices.text: A rollback, done automatically
choices.why: Rolling back is a command somebody runs.

prompt: With the edited prompt, how many tickets were routed correctly?
With the edited prompt, the new ticket among the misses is t___.
hint: Compare the two lists of misses.

prompt: Why does `route.py` print which tickets it missed, not only how many?
hint: Two runs can share a count.

choices.text: A list is shorter to print than a number
choices.why: It is longer; it is also more useful.

choices.text: Equal counts hide different failures
choices.why: Right: here the list shows `t6` as the new miss.

choices.text: The provider charges per missed ticket
choices.why: Nothing is charged per miss.

choices.text: The log has no other way to record a miss
choices.why: The log records every reply whole.

prompt: `c18` and `c30` are the same ticket. What does `guard trace` show that settles why their replies differ?

choices.text: They used different models
choices.why: Both say `llama3.2:3b`.

choices.text: `c30` ran on a different day
choices.why: The trace shows no date for the call; the version is the difference.

choices.text: `c30` was the second try at that ticket
choices.why: There is no retry in `route.py`.

choices.text: Different versions, one never approved
choices.why: Right: `T10` of lesson 13 has its control.

prompt: A larger model, given the friendly sentence, might keep its JSON valid and greet nobody. Would that make the edit safe to ship unreviewed?
hint: What does the lesson say about reading a prompt's effect?

choices.text: Yes, because nothing broke on that model
choices.why: It would still be a different program nobody measured.

choices.text: Yes, as long as the help pages are unchanged
choices.why: The prompt changed; the pages are another file.

choices.text: No, because larger models never follow such sentences
choices.why: Nothing says they never do.

choices.text: No: its effect is measured, not read off it
choices.why: Right: every change is measured and approved.

prompt: Why does `rollback` copy back a stored text rather than having somebody retype the old prompt?
hint: What happens during the first mistake?

choices.text: Retyping makes a second mistake
choices.why: Right: a second mistake made during the first; the stored copy is exactly what was approved.

choices.text: Retyped text cannot be hashed
choices.why: Any text can be hashed; it would just hash differently.

choices.text: The old prompt is too long to retype
choices.why: It is one line; length is not the point.

choices.text: Rollback also restores the call log
choices.why: The log stays as it was, which is how it should be.

prompt: Can `rollback` restore a version that was never approved?

choices.text: Yes, any version that was ever logged
choices.why: It refuses those.

choices.text: Yes, if the person rolling back names themselves
choices.why: No name makes an unapproved version approved.

choices.text: No, so it cannot deploy unreviewed text
choices.why: Right: only approved versions are in the store.

choices.text: No, it only restores the very first version
choices.why: It restores any approved version.

prompt: Match each question a reviewer asks to what answers it.
hint: One item on the right answers none of them.

pairs.right: the diff in the pull request

pairs.left: does it still do its job?
pairs.right: the cases, run against the new version
the register, with a name and a reason

right_distractors: the number of lines in the prompt

prompt: Why does the lesson ask for a pinned, dated model version rather than a name that always means the newest?
hint: Whose schedule would change the model?

choices.text: It changes on the provider's schedule
choices.why: Right: every measurement would be of a model no longer there.

choices.text: Dated versions are cheaper to call
choices.why: Price is not the reason.

choices.text: Newest models refuse JSON schemas
choices.why: Nothing says so.

choices.text: Pinned models need no review when changed
choices.why: A move to a new one goes through the same review.

prompt: Put the steps of changing a prompt safely in order.
items: Edit the prompt in a branch
Run the cases against the new version
A reviewer approves it with a name and a reason
It is deployed, and every call logs its version

prompt: A client complains about a strange reply from last week. What does Tarefa need to answer with certainty which prompt produced it?
hint: One field in each log line.

choices.text: The prompt file as it is today
choices.why: It may have changed since last week.

choices.text: The prompt version logged with that call
choices.why: Right: and the register says who approved it.

choices.text: The model's temperature setting alone
choices.why: That is one part of the picture, not the prompt.

choices.text: The date of the last deployment
choices.why: A file edited by hand changes without a deployment.

prompt: Tarefa edits a help centre page to correct a fee, and changes no prompt. What does `prompts.py status` do, and why does the lesson want that?
hint: The pages are under review too.

choices.text: Nothing, since only prompts are versioned
choices.why: The help centre pages are under review.

choices.text: It reports the page as not approved, exit 1
choices.why: Right: the assistant repeats the page, `T12` of lesson 13.

choices.text: It approves the page, since fees are public
choices.why: Nothing is approved without a name.

choices.text: It rolls the page back to the last approved text
choices.why: Rolling back is a separate command.
